name: Read the Docs
description: Read the Docs is a documentation building and hosting platform that treats documentation like code: it connects to Git repositories, builds docs automatically on every commit, and gives every pull request a live preview.
best_for: Open source and community projects (free tier) as well as commercial and enterprise engineering teams (paid plans starting around $50/month) that want documentation infrastructure handled for them.
features: Git integration with automatic doc builds on every commit
Pull request previews with visual diffs against production
Support for multiple documentation tools, including Sphinx, MkDocs, and Docusaurus
Versioned documentation built automatically from branches or tags
SSO access control via GitHub or GitLab on paid plans
Private repository support via connected Git accounts or SSH keys
llms.txt and Markdown content negotiation for AI tool compatibility

alternatives.name: Docusaurus
alternatives.description: An open source static site generator for building documentation websites with Markdown/MDX and React.
alternatives.best_for: Teams that want full control of their doc site's design and want to self-host the output.

alternatives.name: GitBook
alternatives.description: A knowledge management platform for creating and publishing product and technical documentation.
alternatives.best_for: Teams that want a visual editor with Git sync rather than a static-site build pipeline.

pricing.starting_price: Community: free for open-source projects; Business Basic: $50/month

tiers.name: Community
tiers.notes: Free forever for open-source projects; public, ad-supported documentation hosting.

tiers.name: Business Basic
tiers.notes: 2 concurrent builds, shared domain, GitHub/GitLab SSO, 50 redirects.

tiers.name: Business Advanced
tiers.notes: 4 concurrent builds, 5 custom domains, 250 redirects, 30-day analytics.

tiers.name: Business Pro
tiers.notes: 6 concurrent builds, 15 custom domains, Google SSO, 500 redirects, 90-day analytics.

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.notes: Starts from $10k/year; custom requirements, SAML SSO, dedicated builders, advanced audit tracking, and support SLA.

cons: The free Community service is for open-source projects and uses public, ad-supported hosting; private or commercial documentation belongs on the paid Business service.

Business Basic uses a shared domain and does not include the custom-domain and analytics allowances listed for Advanced and Pro; higher build concurrency and enterprise controls require more expensive tiers.
